h2: Eddy current testing around Chicago: tube bundles, airframes and the outages that schedule them
html:
Eddy current testing around Chicago: tube bundles, airframes and the outages that schedule them

Around Chicago, eddy current testing is mainly tube inspection in refinery and power-plant heat exchangers, plus surface-crack and conductivity work in aircraft maintenance. Tube material and outage windows decide the technique and the timing. Atlantis mobilises ET crews from Houston for exchanger and condenser campaigns, works to ASME Section V Article 8 or the owner's specification, and has every tube map reviewed by an ASNT NDT Level III.

Refinery exchangers. The Joliet refinery's 12 major process units and the CITGO plant at Lemont between them hold thousands of exchanger tubes that come out for inspection at turnaround. Bobbin eddy current suits copper alloy, stainless and titanium tubing; carbon-steel bundles need remote field or near-field screening, with IRIS ultrasonic tube inspection used to size what the screening finds. Getting that split right before the bundles are pulled matters more than any other planning decision, because the wrong probe set costs a shift at the worst point of the outage.

Nuclear and balance of plant. Illinois has 11 reactors at six Constellation stations. Only Braidwood and Byron are pressurized water reactors with steam generators; Clinton, Dresden, LaSalle and Quad Cities are boiling water reactors. Steam generator tubing is examined under the licensee's own qualified programme by specialist vendors, but condensers, feedwater heaters and coolers on every unit still need tube examination during refuelling outages. The turbine replacements planned at Byron and Braidwood through 2029 are being installed during those same outages, so balance-of-plant windows are crowded. State law gives the Illinois Emergency Management Agency jurisdiction over boilers and pressure vessels at nuclear sites.

Aircraft maintenance. AAR Corp., based in Wood Dale, runs a wide-body airframe maintenance base at Chicago Rockford International Airport that began operating at the end of 2016. Eddy current is the routine method there for fastener-hole cracking, surface cracks at radii and conductivity checks after heat damage.

Where the results go. Exchanger shells registered as pressure vessels in Illinois sit on the state's three-year cycle, or on API 510 intervals where a qualified owner-user runs its own programme. Tube results therefore belong in the same equipment record as shell thickness and the last internal visual, so the owner's inspector can see wall-loss trends in one place rather than across separate vendor reports.

What a Chicago ET tube campaign should specify before mobilisation:

  • Tube material, outside diameter, wall thickness and any U-bend or finned sections, so probes and reference standards are made in advance.
  • Whether the owner wants full-bundle screening or a sample plan, and who makes the plugging decision.
  • The reporting format: a tubesheet map and indication list the owner's engineer can act on, delivered into Atlantis NDT reporting or the plant's own system.

The national eddy current testing service lists bobbin, array and rotating-probe options, and turnaround and shutdown inspection explains how crews slot into a refinery outage. Technicians looking for the method course will find eddy current testing training separately. To plan a tube campaign in the Chicago area, share the bundle list.
